steps.page: What you want from review decks
steps.intro: Seven statements you marked in round 9. Reopen any that no longer hold.

steps.path: What I think you want
steps.headline: A deck is where you steer. I decide only what no user could notice.
steps.changed: You decide layout, the path between screens and how parts affect each other. I decide code matters inside those decisions.
steps.notice: A deck never asks you about code, and never settles a design question without you.

steps.path: What I think you want
steps.headline: One feature has one deck, on one link, that grows with the work.
steps.changed: It starts as "here is how I understand this", becomes the design, then the plan before building, then the results after. It is never replaced by a new deck each round.
steps.notice: You keep one link per feature. Opening it always shows where the feature stands now.

steps.path: What I think you want
steps.headline: What you said earlier stays visible where it belongs, not behind a History button.
steps.changed: Each topic shows its own story in place: your words, what was built, what you said next. Settled topics shrink.
steps.notice: No History button, no "Details" fold, no New or Changed badges.

notes: I still haven't completely decided what I want this UI to look like. Um I'm open to it maybe being somewhat hidden or just being kind of sorted to the bottom or uh again, I don't really know. I I I think I want to think through a couple of real use cases first before we decide exactly what this like history or like evolution kind of concept is. Um'cause I could see a world where like I respond to…

steps.resolved: Built the way you picked in round 10: answered topics sink, one line of the past, the rest on request. It is this deck.

steps.path: What I think you want
steps.headline: Every page is named for what you are deciding, never for my work.
steps.changed: Pages like "What the reviewers found" or "What slipped between rounds" describe my process. Pages should be the stages and topics of the feature.
steps.notice: You can tell from a page's name what it wants from you.

steps.path: What I think you want
steps.headline: A card holds one kind of thing: facts, things you can change, or results.
steps.changed: Round 8 mixed plain rows, changeable rows and rows with a Passed or Unclear chip in one card.
steps.notice: Chips appear only on a results page, on every row of it. A question is always its own card with buttons.

steps.path: What I think you want
steps.headline: A deck should look like part of YouCoded, with pictures large enough to read.
steps.changed: Only parts the app already has. You have asked for larger pictures in rounds 4, 5 and 8.
steps.notice: A picture opens at a size where its words can be read without zooming.

steps.path: What I think you want
steps.headline: There is no contract or sign-off deck. The safety checks that came with it should not vanish silently.
steps.changed: Finished means: every request is a row before building, and you change nothing after. The old automatic checks need a home; the "safety net" page asks where.
steps.notice: Fewer decks to sign, without losing what the old checks caught.

notes: I think the the the the the way you phrase this might be a little broad. There is no longer a contract or sign off deck in the old form with the old process. We're obsoleting that and superseding it with something better. Um I do think our pre-build deck is effectively going to serve a similar purpose to the contract deck. the post build deck will serve a similar purpose to the sign off deck. Um…

steps.resolved: Reworded in the rules: the deck before a build takes the old contract's place, the deck after it the old sign-off's, and it says what changed while building.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Tick or change

calls.call: Each row here has a tick and a pencil. Tick means fine; the pencil opens a comment.
calls.why: The pressed one is outlined. There are no "Fine / Change asked / Not looked at" labels.

calls.call: Writing a comment takes the tick off. A row with a comment cannot be ticked until the comment is binned.
calls.why: So a row never says both.

calls.call: Leaving a page approves nothing.
calls.why: Before, a list you left alone counted as accepted.

calls.call: At Done, rows you neither ticked nor changed are listed. You can still send.
calls.why: They reach me as "not looked at", never as approved. You picked "warn" in round 10.

calls.call: After a build, a row you have not looked at keeps the work marked unfinished.
calls.why: Part of the done / not-done check.

calls.call: The label at a list's top right ("3 of 5 looked at") still has the deck's usual small dot.
calls.why: Change this row if the dot should go.

steps.reopened: You asked for one pencil in round 3, then for a way no unread row is ever taken as approved.

trail.asked: simplify down to a single pencil/edit icon on each of these rows

trail.said: i want to eliminate the scenario where a row gets accidentally taken as approved just because i didnt read or see it
i definitely dont like the weird new blue change asked/fine/not looked at indicator things you added
trail.built: A tick and a pencil, with no labels.
